name: Frame clock
responsibility: The clock that motion reads: the browser's own on a live page, a stepped one on a replay
description: The ./frame-clock entry of ui-clocks, moved from ui-kit (TASK-653.17). A replay creates its stepped clock over its window (createSteppedClock(start, window)), which takes over the browser's own requestAnimationFrame at once, so a library's frames run on it too, and swaps it in before it mounts anything (driveFramesFrom). It stands every animation at the frame's time, and syncAnimations returns every violation so far: an animation on a timeline it cannot stand. The picture stage asks it for its frames and reads its time, so a replay steps the canvas too. A lint rule keeps the viewer on it rather than on the browser's timers.
